subject: Map, not set, axis tick labels

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Map, not set, axis tick labels
parts:
Hey everyone,
Is it possible to map to axis tick labels, instead of setting them? My use case is that I am trying to focus attention on just a few discrete labels.

For example,

df <- data.frame(A = letters[1:3], B = 1:3, Is.focus = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE), stringsAsFactors = FALSE);
# This does a good job of highlighting the points in the plot...
p <- ggplot(df, aes(A, B)) + geom_point(aes(alpha = Is.focus), size = 6)
# ...but it would be nice to also map Is.focus to the tick labels as well, something like
p + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(color = "red", face = "bold"))
# where only `a` is red and bold, and `b` and `c` are the defaults

Would an option be to use `element_blank` and then `geom_text`? I am not sure how to get those to line up exactly where the tick marks should be, so any help there is appreciated.

Thanks,
Doug

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Map, not set, axis tick labels
parts:
This isn't a mapping, but rather an ifelse() idiom, which works in
this case because Is.focus is logical:

p + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(color = ifelse(df$Is.focus,
"red", "black"),
face = ifelse(df$Is.focus,
"bold", "plain")))

Dennis

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Re: Map, not set, axis tick labels
parts:
The initial solution worked for my basic plot, but in my real data, I want to facet as well. Unfortunately, that does not work for freed scales, so let me add another wrinkle to this.

df <- data.frame(A = letters[1:3], B = 1:3, Is.focus = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE), Facet = c("X", "X", "Y"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE);
# Works per Dennis's idea
p <- ggplot(df, aes(A, B)) + geom_point(aes(alpha = Is.focus), size = 6) +

# This works...
p + facet_grid(. ~ Facet)
# ...but in my real data I have lots of discrete values, so what I want to work is
p + facet_grid(. ~ Facet, scales = "free_x")
# As you can see, `c` is incorrectly marked as focused.
